verdict.rationale: Fly.io's own site describes running workloads in a hardware-isolated VM with a clean baseline per request, egress-locked and disposable. It also describes Fly Machines as hardware-isolated, sub-second-booting VMs, which covers both the isolation and the disposability parts of the story. The evidence is marketing-level only, and running untrusted code is implied by per-user state isolation rather than stated outright. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on the sandbox security model and lifecycle, explicit untrusted-code guidance, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the isolation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run untrusted code in hardware-isolated, disposable sandboxes

citations.quote: Run it in a hardware-isolated VM. A clean baseline per request, so no two users ever share state. Egress-locked and disposable.
Fly Machines are hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second
Every agent gets its own Linux box.
